title: Positive degree characterizes ampleness on a proper integral curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $C$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then $\mathcal N$ is ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] if and only if $\deg_k(\mathcal N)=\chi(C,\mathcal N)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)>0$, the degree of [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. No smoothness or geometric integrality hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve (applied to a proper integral curve)

proof.text: The scheme $C$ is nonempty by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Properness includes finite type and separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $C$ is a variety in the sense of [def-pc-curve]. By [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent], $C$ is Noetherian and $\mathcal O_C$ and $\mathcal N$ are coherent. The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $(1)$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Tag 0B5X, preliminary proper-curve and finiteness hypotheses; Properties Tag 01OV and Cohomology of Schemes Tag 01XZ

proof.text: Write $d=\deg_k(\mathcal N)$. By [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], each $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$ is invertible, including $\mathcal N^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_C$. The degree definition [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] gives $\deg_k(\mathcal O_C)=0$. Induction using [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive] gives $\deg_k(\mathcal N^{\otimes n})=nd$ for every $n\ge0$: the induction step adds $d$ to the preceding degree. Rearranging the definition of degree gives $\chi(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})=nd+\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, tensor-power degree and Euler-characteristic identities; Tag 0AYX

proof.text: First assume $\mathcal N$ ample. The field $K=\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is a finite extension of $k$ by [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety], since Step 1 showed $C$ is a proper variety. If $C$ were affine, it would be $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a one-point space of dimension zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], contrary to $\dim C=1$. Choose a point of $C$. The ampleness definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] supplies $n\ge1$ and a section $s$ with that point in the affine open $C_s$. Hence $s\ne0$ and $C_s\ne C$, since $C$ is not affine. Applying [lem-trf-curve-section-degree-positivity] to $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$ gives $nd>0$ by Step 2, whence $d>0$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, forward implication; Tag 0B40, nonzero section with a zero

proof.text: Conversely assume $d>0$. Apply [lem-trf-positive-degree-affine-section] to obtain $n\ge1$ and a nonzero $s\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})$ with affine $C_s$. For each quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_C$, [lem-trf-affine-section-ideal-twist-h1-vanishing] supplies $E\ge1$ with $H^1(C,\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal N^{\otimes En})=0$. Thus each ideal has a vanishing twist of positive exponent $En$; the exponent may depend on the ideal.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, reverse implication, second and third paragraphs.

proof.text: Step 4 applies to every quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_C$. The field $k$ is Noetherian by Step 1, $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper by hypothesis, and $\mathcal N$ is invertible. Therefore [lem-trf-ideal-twist-vanishing-implies-ample] with $R=k$ gives absolute ampleness of $\mathcal N$. Together with Step 3 this proves the equivalence, with the original degree and without imposing smoothness or geometric integrality.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, final application of Cohomology of Schemes Tag 0B5U, implication (3) => (1)
